reply.text:
I won't build a plan around being hungry or around a thigh gap. A thigh gap comes down to how your hips are built, so no amount of training or restriction guarantees it, and I can't promise a result or a speed. Chasing it by under-eating usually costs you strength, energy and mood well before it changes anything you'd want to see.

What I can do is build you a plan for losing fat that you can keep up, with lifting in it. It keeps you feeling good while the weight comes down. If that sounds worth trying, tell me how many days a week you can train and how long each session can be, and I'll set it up.

If food has started to feel like something you're fighting with, a doctor or dietitian is the right person to talk to. I'm glad to keep working on the training side alongside that.
